messages:
Alex: quick spike update — tried a slab-splay + page-packing allocator for the paged KV cache. goal: reduce page fragmentation and 99p tail for long chat workloads. rough TL;DR: 99p down ~12% in microbench, avg alloc time up ~0.5-0.8us. tradeoffs below.

Maya: can you paste the microbench and profiler output? also, which attention kernel was this with (flash-attn-v2 / fused)?

Alex: bench was on flash-attn-v2 compiled kernels with kernel-selection disabled (forced v2). config: page_size=64KB, pagepacking_enabled=true, slab_splay_threshold=4. profiler snippet: ```
alloc_path: slab_splay
avg_alloc_us: 1.9 -> baseline 1.2
99p_alloc_us: 12.3 -> baseline 14.1
kv_page_evictions_per_min: 38 -> baseline 52
paged-attn-99p-token-latency: 120ms -> baseline 136ms
overall-throughput: -0.6%
```

Dmitri: interesting. so fewer evictions but higher per-alloc cost. does pagepacking increase contiguous page runs so the block table lookups are faster?

Alex: yeah that's the hypothesis — we keep pages contiguous in virtual slot space more often, so the block-index walk tends to hit sequential entries, which reduces random GPU-to-CPU syncs when filling KV pages. also KV cache probes that consult the LRU table see fewer scattered misses.

Olivia: we need to think about interaction with kernel selection and batching. if kernel router decides to fallback to fused-attn for short sequences, will the allocator keep contiguity assumptions? could be a correctness risk if we rely on ordering for multi-kernel KV pinning.

Maya: also curious about rollback behavior on OOMs. slab-splay seems more complex to free — do we have a safe fallback to the simple slab allocator during emergency?

Alex: implemented a cheap fallback: if reclaim loop fails 3x, set pagepacking_enabled=false for that worker and publish a metric. rollback path verified in local sim. code: ```
if (!reclaim_success) {
  worker.flags.pagepacking_enabled = false;
  metric.increment("pagepacking.rollback");
}
```

Dmitri: any perf regressions on fused-attn benchmarks? we should run the same allocator with kernel-selection enabled and a mixed traffic trace (short+long) so router picks kernels naturally.

Alex: ran a quick mixed trace — with kernel-selection enabled, the 99p benefit drops to ~6% (since many short requests used fused-attn which doesn't touch paged KV as much). overall throughput drop is ~0.4%.

Olivia: that suggests we should gate pagepacking by workload signature or have the kernel router emit hints so allocator can prefer compacting when long-sequence load is expected. also we should add a config to prefer contiguous allocation only for pages marked hot_by_sequence_length.

Maya: agree. can you add a small experiment: pagepacking auto-enable when avg_seq_len_over_1m > 256 and kernel_router.long_seq_frac > 0.2? that would keep costs down for mixed traffic.

Alex: will do. next steps: 1) run mixed-trace A/B with pagepacking auto-gating, 2) perf checks across flash-attn-v1/v2 and fused-attn, 3) add more telemetry on blocktable sequentiality. aiming to push a draft PR tomorrow.

ci-bot: perf-check: draft branch queued. baseline vs draft: 99p token latency -9% (paged-heavy), overall p50 +0.2%, end-to-end throughput -0.6%. see /ci/artifacts/2117654321.

Olivia: awesome. also add a stress test for eviction storms — want to be sure we don't regress stability when the allocator does aggressive packing.

Dmitri: I'll help with the mixed-trace harness and kernel-selection matrix.

Maya: tagging this for the perf sync tomorrow. thanks Alex :thumbsup:
